title: serving runtime weekly update - kernel, KV cache, batching (2026-05-06)
content:
Weekly update: focus on kernel scheduling improvements, KV cache correctness and eviction, and batching policy tuning. This doc captures standup highlights, decisions, blockers, and next steps for the week of 2026-04-30 -> 2026-05-06.

Summary (high level):
- Kernel work: landed selective kernel dispatch for multi-head attention variants (PR 842). Initial microbenchmarks show 12-18% latency reduction for long-sequence (>=2048) generative workloads on A100. Still verifying across sequence-length distribution and XLA path.
- KV cache: fixed a race that could cause stale KV reads during concurrent rollouts; added additional unit tests and integration test harness. Eviction policy adjusted to LRU-with-priority to keep prefixes cached for hot routes.
- Batching: tuned dynamic batcher to favor latency SLO routes by lowering max batch window to 6ms for p50 sensitive endpoints; throughput routes retain 15-20ms window. Measured 8% throughput drop on non-SLO tests but 22% p95 latency improvement for SLO routes.

Standup notes (daily):
- Mon (2026-04-30): Kernel team: validated kernel selection logic for qkv-fused vs qkv-split on 8k seq; some divergence in perf on older drivers (470.x). Action: add driver detection and fallback. KV team: repro of rollback bug on Dedicated clusters; created JIRA-INF-2143. Batching: started A/B on internal staging 2, phase A uses 6ms window for chat API.
- Tue (2026-05-01): Kernel: merged PR 842 to main, rolled out to canary. Observed a regression on short sequences (<128) for small models (7B float16) — higher CPU overhead in dispatch. Action: add size threshold to keep old path for small models. KV: added integration test that replays 48h production traffic. Found edge case when route remapping and cache invalidation coincide.
- Wed (2026-05-02): Incident drill: KV prune job hit higher IO causing tail latency spikes on a Dedicated node. Mitigation: throttle prune job and move to background priority. Batching: telemetry shows reduced p95 but token utilization decreased for throughput customers. Noted customers flagged throughput drop in synthetic load test.
- Thu (2026-05-03): Performance lab: rebench kernels on latest driver (520.x) and CUDA 12.3. Gains are consistent; added automated driver matrix to CI. KV: implemented LRU-with-priority policy prototype; initial results keep warm prefixes 4x longer.
- Fri (2026-05-06): Retro + planning: decision to ship kernel dispatch in release-3.8 behind feature flag with size/driver heuristics. KV fixes will be rolled as hotfix to stable and staged to Dedicated next week. Batching changes to be opt-in via route config under /account-level settings so customers can opt into latency-preserving windows.

Metrics & benchmarks: (representative)
- Kernel microbench (A100, seq=2048, model=13B): baseline p50=120ms -> new dispatch p50=102ms (15%); p95 improved 10%.
- Small model regressions: 7B, seq=64: baseline p50=18ms -> new dispatch p50=22ms (regression) until size-threshold applied.
- Batching AB test: SLO route p95 down from 380ms -> 298ms; overall throughput drop ~8% in synthetic test.
- KV cache hit rate: +6% for top-50 routes after priority LRU; background prune reduced cache size churn by 32%.

Decisions made this week:
- Ship kernel-select dispatch in release-3.8 behind feature flag. Default off for small models and older drivers. (Owner: Miguel)
- Roll out KV race fix as hotfix to stable and Dedicated clusters next Tuesday (2026-05-12). Add IO-throttling to prune job. (Owner: Evelyn)
- Expose batching window per-route in console; default conservative values for managed accounts; opt-in for PLG customers who want aggressive latency tuning. (Owner: Benji + Console team)

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Miguel: add driver-detection & size threshold heuristics to kernel dispatch (PR follow-up) — ETA: 2026-05-10.
- Evelyn: finalize KV integration test harness, add CI job that replays 24h prod traffic daily, and schedule dedicated hotfix rollout — ETA: 2026-05-12.
- Benji: implement per-route batching controls in console and route-config API; add migration guide for customers — ETA: 2026-05-20.
- Claire: run extended perf sweep across available HW matrix (A100, H100, V100) and report anomalies into perf-dashboard — ETA: 2026-05-14.
- Asha: update release notes draft and call out feature-flag instructions & known regressions — ETA: 2026-05-08.

Blockers & risks:
- Driver compatibility: older CUDA/driver combinations (470.x) show regressions; need robust detection and safe fallback to avoid customer impact.
- KV IO: prune job can interfere with tail latency on smaller Dedicated instances. Throttling helps but we need long-term redesign of prune scheduling.
- Customer opt-in friction: exposing batching controls is powerful but may confuse PLG users. Need clear defaults and docs.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adaptive batching that learns per-route latency curve and adjusts window automatically instead of manual knob. Prototype in staging after console rollout.
- Add telemetry tag for kernel-path used in each request to make post-mortem easier.
- Evaluate prioritized eviction based on business metric (route-weight * recency) instead of pure LRU.

Links / references: see linked_artifacts above for PR/Confluence. Also look at perf-dashboard charts: perf/redwood/serving/runtime/release-3.8/ (internal).

Next week plan (brief):
- Finish kernel heuristics and complete canary validation.
- Hotfix KV and deploy to Dedicated staging, monitor for IO tail.
- Console batching controls MVP + docs.
- Perf matrix sweep and finalize release notes.

If you want deeper dive on any of the items (kernel microbench results, KV integration logs, or batching AB test data) I can paste the specific tables/graphs into this doc or link the dashboards.

-- Asha
